issues.legal_issue: A tenant seeking adjustment of rent paid in excess of the statutory standard rent must use the statutory refund or adjustment procedure within the prescribed period.
material_facts: The tenant had paid rent at a rate above the rate it later claimed was the applicable standard rent.
In a landlord’s suit for unpaid rent, the tenant sought to adjust the earlier excess payments against the rent claimed.
The tenant had not applied to the designated rent authority for a refund or adjustment within six months of the payments.
issues.conclusion: The tenant could not obtain adjustment of the earlier excess payments against the rent claimed in the suit because it had not followed the statutory procedure within the prescribed period.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(10), 3, 7, 9, 11 and 17 of the West Bengal Premises Rent Control (Temporary Provisions) Act, 1950 governed the determination and irrecoverability of rent above the standard rent. Section 7 provided for an application to the Controller for refund or adjustment within six months of payment or deposit. A claim relying on the Act’s protection against excess rent could not be separated from the procedure and time limit the Act prescribed for obtaining a refund or adjustment. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: arrears_suit and tenant_claims_adjustment_for_excess_rent and statutory_refund_or_adjustment_procedure_applies and not timely_application_to_rent_authority

predicates.arrears_suit: A landlord brought a proceeding to recover rent that the tenant had not paid.
predicates.tenant_claims_adjustment_for_excess_rent: The tenant sought to apply rent previously paid above the lawful standard against the amount claimed by the landlord.
predicates.statutory_refund_or_adjustment_procedure: A governing rent-control regime provides a procedure for obtaining a refund or adjustment of rent paid above the lawful standard.
predicates.timely_application_to_rent_authority: The tenant applied to the designated rent authority for a refund or adjustment within the time allowed after making the relevant payment.

issues.definition: If a tenant in an arrears suit seeks adjustment of excess rent under a regime that provides a refund or adjustment procedure but did not apply to the rent authority in time, the adjustment is denied.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant cannot use a general-law set-off to bypass an applicable statutory procedure for recovering or adjusting excess rent.
material_facts: The tenant relied on the rent-control legislation to claim that earlier payments above the standard rent were irrecoverable.
The tenant also suggested that it could claim a set-off under general law, but had not laid a proper foundation for that contention at the earlier stages of the case.
The legislation provided a procedure for seeking refund or adjustment of the excess payments, which the tenant had not followed in time.
issues.conclusion: The general-law set-off contention could not be entertained and had no merit because the tenant could not rely on selected provisions of the special legislation while disregarding its applicable refund or adjustment procedure.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Section 7 of the West Bengal Premises Rent Control (Temporary Provisions) Act, 1950, which prescribed the procedure and time limit for seeking refund or adjustment of sums paid that were irrecoverable under the Act. Where a right and its remedy are provided by the same statute, the remedy cannot be dissociated from the right. The contention also lacked a proper foundation at the earlier stages. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: appellate_proceeding and excess_rent_claimed_under_special_rent_regime and statutory_recovery_procedure_applies and no_proper_foundation_for_general_setoff

predicates.appellate_proceeding: A party raised or pursued the set-off contention in an appeal.
predicates.excess_rent_claimed_under_special_rent_r: A party relied on a special rent-control regime to claim that rent previously paid above the lawful standard was recoverable or adjustable.
predicates.statutory_recovery_procedure_applies: The special rent-control regime prescribes a procedure for recovering or adjusting the excess payment.
predicates.no_proper_foundation_for_general_setoff: The party did not properly raise and support its general-law set-off contention at the earlier stages of the case.

issues.definition: When a party pursuing an appeal relies on a special rent regime that prescribes a recovery procedure but lacks a proper foundation for a general-law set-off, the general-law set-off is not entertained.

issues.legal_issue: The statutory restitution remedy for a payment made by mistake is unavailable when mistake in making the payment has not been proved.
material_facts: The tenant invoked the rule governing money paid by mistake to support its claim concerning earlier rent payments.
The appellate court had found, on its assessment of the evidence, that no mistake in making the excess payments had been proved.
The Supreme Court relied on that finding in rejecting the tenant’s reliance on the restitution rule.
issues.conclusion: The tenant could not obtain relief under Section 72 of the Contract Act because mistake in making the payments had not been proved.
issues.legal_principle: Section 72 of the Contract Act concerns money paid by mistake. The Court held that it could not assist the tenant in light of the appellate court’s finding that no mistake had been proved. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.claim_for_restitution_of_rent_payment: A payer sought restitution of rent previously paid on the ground that the payment was mistaken.
predicates.mistake_in_payment_proved: The payer established that the relevant payment was made by mistake.

issues.definition: If a payer seeks restitution of rent on the ground of mistake but does not prove a mistake in payment, mistake-based restitution is unavailable.
